_note: Plain-English readings of the second-level sub-themes, written after reading representative
passages rather than inferred from the term lists. Each entry names an exemplar by passage_id;
scripts/build_second_level_report.py pulls that passage's text out of the corpus at render time,
so no quote in the report is ever hand-transcribed. A reading is our interpretation and is
labelled as such; the quote beneath it is the filing's own words.
Sub-theme ids are local to their parent model. topic_1 here means the first sub-theme of the
named parent, not the parent model's topic_1.

topic_1.label: Tax definitions and cost accounting
topic_1.reading: Tax definition clauses and cost-of-sales discussion. It is drawn in by words like payroll, severance and withholding, but most of it is not employee-terms language at all. It fails the stability bar, and it is the clearest sign that parent Theme 1 was carrying material that does not belong to it.

topic_2.label: Executive roles and board governance
topic_2.reading: Who holds which office and how the board is composed: chief executive succession, chairman restrictions, voting agreements over board seats. This is corporate governance around named executives rather than the terms of their employment, and it is the largest and most stable part of the theme.

topic_3.label: Collective bargaining and works councils
topic_3.reading: Labour-relations representations in merger agreements: whether the target is party to a collective bargaining agreement, whether a works council represents its employees, whether a representation campaign is under way. The most coherent sub-theme anywhere in this study, and conceptually nothing to do with executives. It fails the stability bar because it is small and concentrated in the deals that happen to have unionised or European workforces.

topic_1.label: Closing payment mechanics
topic_1.reading: Purchase-price definitions, escrow releases, flow-of-funds memoranda, and closing bonus and unit-appreciation payments routed through payroll. Much of this is transaction-consideration language that mentions employees rather than employee-terms language, which is why it is the least coherent of the three and the only one to fail the stability bar.

topic_2.label: Standing equity plans and new grants
topic_2.reading: The equity programme as it already exists: the incentive plan, grants made to named executives, unit counts and vesting schedules. It describes the plan rather than what the acquisition does to it.

topic_3.label: Award treatment at the effective time
topic_3.reading: What happens to each option and RSU at closing: assumed, converted into an acquirer award, accelerated, or cancelled for no consideration. This is the sub-theme closest to the research question, and it is both the most coherent and the most stable of the three.
